new_scholarship.name: Eric Bleumink Fellowship
new_scholarship.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of a listed group of countries who hold provisional or unconditional admission to a one or two year master's programme starting in September. The grant covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. It is nomination-based: the University of Groningen's Admission Office decides which admitted applicants are nominated, so there is no direct scholarship application. The University of Groningen states that a considerable number of students apply each year while it can issue only a limited number of grants.

new_scholarship.deadline: There is no scholarship application deadline: "It is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship Scholarship. Suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination." Applicants must hold a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February, and their master's application "should be completed by the applicant before 1st of December".

new_scholarship.official_source: Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV)
new_scholarship.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.

Selection for the annual programme takes place twice a year via an Open Call.
new_scholarship.application_period: Open Call, selection twice a year. Eight three-month fellowships are available each year across four periods: March-May, June-August, September-November and December-February. The next call is published in September 2026 and closes 14 October 2026.

No university or research institute affiliation is required, but fellows must have a steady income during the fellowship.

new_scholarship.name: Tilburg University Waiver
new_scholarship.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.

Outcomes are notified by June 1, 2027.

new_scholarship.name: Radboud Scholarship Programme
new_scholarship.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a highly selective Radboud University scheme for talented, highly motivated non-EU/non-EEA students with outstanding study results, covering English-taught Master's programmes. A scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (the university notes the amount is to be confirmed) instead of an illustrative EUR 19,000, and additionally covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs. Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028, allocated across six faculties, and selection is based on academic excellence, ambition and the quality of two reference letters.

Final decisions are notified before mid-April 2027.

new_scholarship.name: University of Amsterdam Scholarships
new_scholarship.description: The University of Amsterdam runs several scholarship programmes for talented and motivated international students, published from one official Fees and funding hub. The flagship is the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA planning a Master's programme at the UvA. Each faculty also runs its own scholarships for international Master's students, covering Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Science and Social and Behavioural Sciences, and a separate set of Bachelor's scholarships exists. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship equals the tuition fee but the UvA states it cannot be used as a partial tuition waiver, so the recipient still pays the full tuition, payable in monthly instalments. Amounts are set annually and are published by each faculty.

Deadlines are set per scheme and per faculty: faculty scholarship pages for the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship give an application deadline of 15 January, with results announced at the end of April, while some faculties run a later round with a 2 February deadline. Amounts are determined each year and published in late autumn.

new_scholarship.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
